Among very patient firms the number of market makers hardly matters, because the threat of losing future profits holds even large cartels together. The dip at the most patient end appears to come from a modelling simplification in markets with a minimum price step (an investigation that finds nothing is treated as worse for firms than a conviction): patient firms weigh heavily the ordinary earnings that such an investigation wipes out.

That help matters most among impatient firms and almost disappears once firms are patient enough to hold the cartel together anyway. That late fall appears to be a modelling simplification in markets with a minimum price step (an investigation that finds nothing is treated as worse for firms than a conviction), not a real effect of patience: it disappears when every investigation ends in a conviction.
